title: Perf suite: add mixed prompt-length scenarios + baseline comparison harness
author: Rina Kobayashi
body:
Context
This PR updates the runtime perf suite to cover mixed prompt-length distributions (short/interactive mixed with long/prefill-heavy prompts) and introduces a baseline comparison harness so we can gate scheduler changes with stable, repeatable A/B results.

This is part of the mixed-workload scheduler prototype effort (ENG-4825). The scheduler work needs a consistent way to answer: does short traffic p95 improve under mixed load, without unacceptable throughput regression or long-prompt starvation?

What’s in this PR
1) New benchmark scenarios (mixed prompt-length distributions)
- Adds scenario definitions that model common mixed workloads:
  - mixed_80_20: 80% short / 20% long
  - mixed_50_50: 50% short / 50% long
  - mixed_bursty_short: short burst overlay on background long prompts
  - mixed_long_heavy: long prompts dominate (stress fairness + backpressure)
- Each scenario defines:
  - prompt length distribution (tokens)
  - arrival pattern (Poisson, burst windows)
  - concurrency targets
  - streaming on/off mode (where applicable)
  - fixed output token targets to isolate prefill vs decode effects

2) Baseline comparison harness (A/B runner)
- Adds a small harness that runs the exact same scenario twice:
  - baseline: scheduler flag off (or current default)
  - candidate: scheduler flag on / variant under test
- Emits a standardized comparison table:
  - p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency
  - prefill vs decode breakdown (when available from metrics)
  - throughput (tok/s) and request/s
  - GPU utilization proxy signals (from perf runner stats)
  - queueing signals (when present) as informational (not gating yet)

3) CI gating defaults for mixed workloads
- Adds perf pipeline thresholds for the new scenarios:
  - short class: p95 must not regress vs baseline; improvement expected but not enforced as a gate in this PR
  - overall throughput: allow small regression bounded by scenario (defaults: <= 3% regression)
  - stability: adds minimum iteration count and warmup to reduce run-to-run variance
- Important: these gates are only enabled in the “runtime-perf” lane and are tagged as mixed_workload so we can disable quickly if they cause noise.

4) Documentation + operator notes (bench runner)
- Updates perf suite README with:
  - how to run the new scenarios locally
  - how to run baseline vs candidate comparisons
  - notes on controlling confounders (warmup, batch size caps, seed)

Implementation notes / rationale
- Distributions are token-based rather than char-based. Prompt inputs are generated deterministically from tokenized templates to reduce variance across runner versions.
- Long prompts are defined by prompt_tokens >= 2048 by default in these scenarios; the value is intentionally conservative and aligns with how we’ve been testing the scheduler prototype so far.
- The harness is intentionally thin and uses existing runner primitives. It is not a general experiment framework; it’s just enough to get repeatable A/B numbers for scheduler work.

Example output (abbreviated)
Scenario: mixed_80_20 (A100-80GB, batch cap=??)
- baseline p95 (short): 410ms
- candidate p95 (short): 290ms
- baseline throughput: 100%
- candidate throughput: 98.5%

(Real numbers will vary by hardware + model; above is illustrative and not meant as a claim for this PR.)

Testing
- Local: ran mixed_80_20 and mixed_50_50 A/B on dev A100 box, verified runner determinism (same seed => same prompt set) and output schema.
- CI: runtime-perf lane updated; new scenarios are included but only as part of the perf suite job (no unit test impact).

Rollout / follow-ups
- ENG-4830 will attach trace-based replays to this harness once we have sanitized traces ready.
- Once scheduler metrics (queue wait histograms, etc.) land, we can promote additional gates (e.g., max long wait bound) in a subsequent PR.

Notes for reviewers
- Please focus review on (a) scenario definitions realism, (b) threshold sanity, and (c) harness determinism / avoidance of measurement artifacts. I kept the harness intentionally simple; if you think it’s missing a critical signal we should gate on now, call it out explicitly.
commits: perf: add mixed prompt-length scenario definitions
perf: implement baseline vs candidate comparison runner
perf: add summary table + JSON output schema for comparisons
ci/perf: wire mixed_workload scenarios into runtime-perf lane with thresholds
docs: update perf suite README with mixed workload usage
review_conversation: Jonas Weber: The scenario set looks good. Two asks: (1) please add a bursty case where short traffic spikes while long is steady, and (2) can we make the throughput regression bound scenario-specific? 3% might be too strict for long-heavy.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Added mixed_bursty_short scenario and moved throughput bounds into per-scenario thresholds (long-heavy now allows up to 5% while others stay 3%). Pushed commits 3c9f1a2 and 7b1140e.
Claire Dubois: Determinism question: are we pinning the prompt set across baseline/candidate and across iterations? Also, please ensure warmup is excluded from summary stats.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Yes—prompt set is generated once per run from a fixed seed and reused for both baseline and candidate. Warmup iterations are now explicitly excluded from reported percentiles; added a guard to fail if warmup==total.

Omar El-Sayed: Can we include prefill/decode split in the comparison output even if it’s best-effort? That will help us catch cases where improvements are from changing decode batching rather than fixing prefill blocking.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Added best-effort prefill/decode extraction when metrics are present; otherwise fields are emitted as 'n/a' to keep schema stable. See output_schema.py updates.
Sahana Iyer: CI gating: please make sure mixed_workload gates are tagged and can be disabled without reverting. Also request to add a short note on how to rerun perf job with candidate flag on.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Added 'mixed_workload' tag and a CI param to disable gates. Updated docs with rerun instructions + example command line.
Grace Kim: Minor: YAML formatting + comments are inconsistent across scenarios. Please align and add a note about max prompt tokens per model so we don’t accidentally exceed context.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Aligned formatting and added a context-limit note per scenario header; runner now clamps generated prompts to model context length and logs when clamping occurs.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Jonas Weber (commit: 9f2c6d7).
